content.text:
## Baseline result

The heuristic router reduces estimated input-side cost from **$87.4229 to $76.5781**, saving **$10.8448 (12.4%)**.

| Route | Trajectories | Estimated savings |
|---|---:|---:|
| Claude Opus 5 → Sonnet 5 | 162 | $5.2938 |
| Claude Fable 5 → Sonnet 5 | 32 | $2.7374 |
| GPT-5.6 Sol → Luna | 24 | $1.4048 |
| Claude Opus 4.8 → Sonnet 5 | 29 | $0.9422 |
| GPT-5.6 Terra → Luna | 20 | $0.4440 |
| Claude Opus 4.6 → Sonnet 5 | 1 | $0.0226 |

The policy rerouted **268 of 953 trajectories (28.1%)**, representing **268 of 1,000 requests (26.8%)**. Every selected trajectory happened to contain a single call.

## Policy

Trajectories below **15,000 estimated aggregate input tokens** are assigned entirely to the cheapest model in the same family:

- Claude → `claude-sonnet-5`
- GPT → `gpt-5.6-luna`

Larger trajectories and those already using the cheapest sibling remain unchanged. Whole-trajectory routing avoids introducing cache-reset penalties from mid-trajectory model switches.

## Important interpretation

This is a credible **cost floor**, not a validated cost–quality result:

- Tokens are estimated as serialized characters divided by four; no measured usage exists.
- Costs include input tokens only; output cost is unknown and excluded.
- Cached input is inferred from exact item-level prefix overlap.
- There is **no outcome or quality estimate** demonstrating that cheaper models preserve task success.
- The frontier’s `quality_placeholder` is merely the fraction of calls kept on the logged model. It is not a quality score and is additionally distorted by 19 reconstructed mixed-model trajectories.
- The router exploits prompt size and model family only, not task structure or recovered outcomes.

I’m grounding the plan in the repo’s existing learned router, evaluation scripts, tests, and presentation workflow first. Then I’ll ask only the product/research choices the code and data cannot answer—especially what “quality” should mean and how aggressive the frontier should be. I’m using the `make-presentation` workflow because the five-minute defense is part of the deliverable.

The key repo finding is more consequential than the current router: the newer `decompose.py` argues that each JSONL row is actually a complete agent trajectory, not one request, yielding about 10.8k call boundaries and recoverable final assistant outputs. That conflicts with the starter brief’s reconstruction premise, so I’m validating it directly against item sequences before we choose the evaluation design; the winning plan should make this discrepancy an explicit, defensible finding rather than silently trust either interpretation.

content.text:
What the repo already supports: a size/tool-count/call-count bucket router with a weak heuristic outcome, a cache-aware price model, a trajectory decomposer, matched-cohort views, and an offline explorer. Its current “learned” result is not defensible yet—it reports 53% below logged input-side cost but relies on in-sample fitting, a placeholder frontier, and the disputed 953-trajectory reconstruction.

Direct inspection favors the newer interpretation: all 1,000 rows are unique, all end in an assistant message, and their item sequences decompose into 10,845 model turns (median 6, max 151). I’d build the next version around that evidence, with a sensitivity analysis for the official wording. Three choices will set the research direction.

questions.question: Which objective should define the router’s selected operating point?

options.label: Quality-constrained cost (Recommended)
options.description: Minimize cache-aware dollars while requiring the estimated failure-rate increase to stay within a small held-out non-inferiority margin.

options.label: Frontier only
options.description: Present multiple policies without selecting a single production operating point.

options.label: Maximum savings
options.description: Optimize cost aggressively and accept a larger, explicitly quantified quality-risk estimate.

questions.question: How should we handle the observed export structure conflicting with the briefing’s one-row-per-call description?

options.label: Dual analysis (Recommended)
options.description: Use the empirically supported row-as-trajectory decomposition and show a sensitivity appendix under the official interpretation.

options.label: Observed structure
options.description: Treat each row as a complete trajectory and make the schema correction a headline insight.

options.label: Official wording
options.description: Keep the current cross-row reconstruction despite weak prefix evidence.

questions.question: Should the plan assume judge-model calls will become available for final evaluation?

options.label: Offline plus optional judge (Recommended)
options.description: Make every result reproducible offline, then add judge scores only as a secondary robustness check if credits arrive.

options.label: Offline only
options.description: Use recovered tool outcomes and completion/error signals with no external model dependence.

options.label: Judge primary
options.description: Use model-based rescoring as the main quality measure and treat offline signals as validation.

content.text:
The direction is now: minimize cache-aware cost subject to a held-out quality constraint; stay fully reproducible offline; use any judge credits only as corroboration; and explicitly report both dataset interpretations.

The next design decision is how much evidence we require before claiming “quality kept.” The observable signals are imperfect: tool errors can be external, final-message language can overclaim success, and retry count is partly task difficulty. A small stratified human audit would calibrate those proxies far better than regex alone. I also need to lock whether the router may make one cache-breaking escalation during a run.

questions.question: How much manual outcome labeling can the team realistically do for proxy calibration?

options.label: 100 trajectories (Recommended)
options.description: Two teammates independently label a stratified 100-run sample and resolve disagreements, giving a credible offline validation set.

options.label: 50 trajectories
options.description: Cuts labeling time but produces wider uncertainty and weaker subgroup checks.

options.label: No manual labels
options.description: Rely entirely on automatic proxies and optional judge scores, with a correspondingly weaker quality claim.

questions.question: What maximum held-out increase in failure rate should define the selected route?

options.label: 2 percentage points (Recommended)
options.description: Use a one-sided 95% upper confidence bound and select the cheapest policy whose degradation stays at or below 2 points.

options.label: 1 percentage point
options.description: A stricter claim that may leave too little statistical power to beat the baseline.

options.label: 5 percentage points
options.description: Enables larger savings but is harder to defend as preserving quality.

questions.question: Should candidate policies be allowed to switch models within a trajectory?

options.label: At most one escalation (Recommended)
options.description: Start cheap when safe, escalate once on observable risk, and never downgrade; explicitly charge the cache reset.

options.label: One model per trajectory
options.description: Maximizes cache reuse and makes off-policy evaluation cleaner, but offers less call-level routing insight.

options.label: Free per-call switching
options.description: Allows more flexibility but creates repeated cache resets and the least defensible counterfactual estimate.

Locked: a context-aware router may start cheap and escalate once, never downgrade; the chosen point must keep the one-sided 95% upper bound on estimated failure degradation within 2 percentage points. With no manual labels, the quality claim must be phrased as “proxy quality” unless optional judge agreement is available—I’ll make that limitation prominent rather than imply ground truth.

One more hard finding resolves model scope: tool dialect and model family are perfectly confounded in this export—Claude trajectories use `bash/file_edit`, while GPT trajectories use `shell_command/apply_patch`. A cross-family quality estimate has no common support and would be indefensible. The router should therefore infer the harness from available tools and optimize only within its family; rare legacy models remain comparators, not routing targets.

There is also a fundamental limit: because the logged model generated the evolving context, an alternative cheap model could have produced a different state before an escalation. Offline data cannot fully identify that sequential counterfactual. We can either make that the honest centerpiece or accept a weaker conditional claim.

# Routermaxxer — Context-Aware Router and Honest Evaluation

## Summary

Build a family-preserving router that minimizes estimated cache-aware cost while keeping the one-sided 95% upper confidence bound on proxy failure degradation within **2 percentage points**.

The primary, defensible frontier assigns one model to the whole trajectory. A secondary adaptive mode may start cheaply and escalate once based on the evolving context; its quality estimate will be labeled conditional because alternative earlier outputs could have changed that context.

Lead the presentation with the empirical data correction: the 1,000 rows behave like complete trajectories containing **10,845 model turns**, not 1,000 independent calls. Retain a sensitivity analysis under the official one-row-per-call interpretation.

## Implementation

- Fast-forward from `origin/main` first and preserve the untracked `initial_context/` directory.
- Make decomposition canonical:
  - Identify maximal runs of model-authored items as calls.
  - Assign stable content-hash trajectory and call IDs.
  - Count tool schemas on every request.
  - Under the official-brief sensitivity mode, discard the final model span and treat its output as unobservable.
- Use estimated JSON characters/4 throughout, explicitly labeled as estimates.
- Calculate cost as uncached input, cached prefix reads, and recovered output tokens. A model change invalidates the entire existing cache.
- Report two cost estimates:
  - Fixed-shape repricing, holding logged token lengths and control flow constant.
  - Behavior-adjusted sensitivity using cross-fitted model-specific output/context-length ratios. Savings must remain positive under its upper cost bound.

### Router policy

Expose a pure decision interface through `scripts/routermaxxer.py`:

```text
choose_model(input_items, tools, default_model, state, mode)
    -> {model, reason_codes, risk_by_model, in_support, escalated}
```

- Infer family from the tool dialect and never cross families because family and harness have no overlap:
  - Claude candidates: Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Fable 5.
  - GPT candidates: Luna, Terra, Sol.
  - Legacy models remain logged comparators but are not routing targets.
- Never use the logged model as a predictive feature; use it only for cost comparison and safe fallback.
- Use interpretable pre-decision features:
  - Opening task intent, trigger type, toolset, image presence, initial size, and surface.
  - At later calls: call position, context growth, previous output kind, prior tool errors, repeated actions, last tool family, user follow-ups, and prospective cache-reset cost.
  - Never use future tool choices, outputs, trajectory depth, or other post-decision data.
- Fit regularized logistic models for model-specific proxy failure and multinomial propensities. Export coefficients and reason codes so every decision is explainable.
- `certified` mode chooses the cheapest supported model at call zero whose estimated quality meets the 2-point constraint and retains it.
- `adaptive` mode applies the same opening choice, then may escalate once when the cheaper model moves outside the quality bound or common support. It never downgrades afterward.
- Unknown toolsets, unsupported contexts, or missing features fall back to `default_model`.

## Quality and Off-Policy Evaluation

- Define the offline binary failure proxy before fitting:
  - Terminal assistant response contains failure, refusal, or inability language.
  - A terminal tool error remains unresolved.
  - The run enters a repeated identical-action failure loop.
- Report the components separately alongside the composite so arbitrary weighting cannot hide regressions.
- Use deterministic 70/30 public train/validation splits grouped by reliable thread key, falling back to trajectory ID. Use the organizer’s held-out split unchanged when it arrives.
- Estimate whole-trajectory outcomes with cross-fitted augmented inverse-propensity weighting:
  - Evaluate only within family.
  - Require proposed-action propensity of at least 0.05, at least 20 observed trajectories, and weighted effective sample size of at least 15.
  - Route unsupported cases to the default model and report coverage.
  - Use 2,000 trajectory-cluster bootstrap replicates for cost, failure difference, and one-sided 95% bounds.
- Select thresholds on training data only. Evaluate the locked policy once on validation and once on the organizer-held-out split.
- Build the headline frontier from certified policies with different quality thresholds and adoption coverage. Select the cheapest point whose failure-degradation upper bound is ≤0.02.
- Show adaptive results as a second series:
  - Price the one allowed cache reset exactly.
  - Label its quality estimate “conditional on logged states.”
  - Do not claim end-to-end non-inferiority for adaptive mode unless optional counterfactual replay supports it.
- If judge credits arrive, replay 120 stratified validation calls near the escalation boundary through the proposed alternative model and have a blinded judge compare logged versus alternative responses. Treat this as robustness evidence, not a required dependency.
- Compare against logged behavior, the corrected heuristic baseline, certified Routermaxxer, adaptive Routermaxxer, and a naive cache-unaware estimate.
- If no policy beats the corrected baseline while satisfying the bound, report that result rather than relaxing the quality criterion.

### Output contracts

Write `results/routermaxxer/` artifacts containing:

- A call ledger with IDs, split, logged/chosen models, mode, reason codes, propensities, support status, risks, switch count, and logged/routed cost.
- A frontier CSV with coverage, cost, savings, proxy failure, degradation, upper confidence bound, and effective sample size.
- A machine-readable evaluation summary containing dataset interpretation, token estimator, cost assumptions, exclusions, and failure modes.

## Tests and Acceptance

- Unit-test call boundaries, stable IDs, prefix caching, output costing, final-output sensitivity, proxy outcomes, feature leakage, family constraints, support fallbacks, and the one-switch invariant.
- Test that a switch charges the complete accumulated prefix uncached and that adaptive mode can never downgrade or switch twice.
- Use synthetic fixtures for known treatment effects to verify propensity weighting, doubly robust estimates, bootstrap intervals, and policy selection.
- Run an offline end-to-end test proving all 1,000 rows map to stable trajectories and approximately 10,845 calls without parse errors.
- Acceptance requires:
  - Deterministic laptop execution in minutes with no GPU or API key.
  - Every displayed number traceable to a generated artifact.
  - No dataset or archive committed.
  - The chosen held-out point satisfies the 2-point upper-bound rule and improves cost over the corrected baseline.
  - Both row interpretations and the sequential counterfactual limitation appear in the report.

## Five-Minute Presentation

Use the Viktor template and brand colors for **routermaxxer**, credited to Atahan Kılıç, Musa Kocabasoğlu, and Utku Kalkanlı.

1. Title: one held-out claim, populated only after the final run.
2. Objective: cheapest route with ≤2-point proxy-quality degradation.
3. Signal: show a real context evolving from cheap start toward escalation.
4. Frontier: one certified headline chart, with adaptive mode visually secondary.
5. Honesty: row-semantics discrepancy, common-support exclusions, proxy-label weakness, and unidentified post-switch states.
6. Close: one number, one claim, one known weakness, and the optional judge-replay next step.

Assumptions: no manual labels; automatic quality remains explicitly a proxy. Organizer schema or pricing corrections override repository assumptions. The optional judge path must not affect offline reproducibility.

+                    trajectories.append(trajectory_from_row(json.loads(line), len(trajectories)))
+    return trajectories

+def _sigmoid(value: float) -> float:
+    if value >= 0:
+        z = math.exp(-min(value, 40.0))
+        return 1.0 / (1.0 + z)
+    z = math.exp(max(value, -40.0))
+    return z / (1.0 + z)
+
+
+class BinaryLogit:
+    """Small deterministic L2 logistic regression for the offline laptop path."""
+
+    def __init__(self, l2: float = 2.0, iterations: int = 1_200):
+        self.l2, self.iterations, self.weights = l2, iterations, []
+
+    def fit(self, xs: Sequence[Sequence[float]], ys: Sequence[int]) -> "BinaryLogit":
+        if not xs:
+            raise ValueError("cannot fit empty outcome model")
+        self.weights = [0.0] * len(xs[0])
+        n = len(xs)
+        for step in range(self.iterations):
+            gradient = [0.0] * len(self.weights)
+            for x, y in zip(xs, ys):
+                error = _sigmoid(sum(w * v for w, v in zip(self.weights, x))) - y
+                for j, value in enumerate(x):
+                    gradient[j] += error * value
+            rate = 0.35 / math.sqrt(1.0 + step / 80.0)
+            for j in range(len(self.weights)):
+                penalty = 0.0 if j == 0 else self.l2 * self.weights[j]
+                self.weights[j] -= rate * (gradient[j] + penalty) / n
+        return self
+
+    def predict(self, x: Sequence[float]) -> float:
+        return min(max(_sigmoid(sum(w * v for w, v in zip(self.weights, x))), 0.001), 0.999)
+
+
+class Softmax:
+    """Deterministic multinomial propensity model."""
+
+    def __init__(self, labels: Sequence[str], l2: float = 2.0, iterations: int = 1_000):
+        self.labels = list(labels)
+        self.l2, self.iterations, self.weights = l2, iterations, []
+
+    def fit(self, xs: Sequence[Sequence[float]], ys: Sequence[str]) -> "Softmax":
+        self.weights = [[0.0] * len(xs[0]) for _ in self.labels]
+        n = len(xs)
+        for step in range(self.iterations):
+            gradients = [[0.0] * len(xs[0]) for _ in self.labels]
+            for x, y in zip(xs, ys):
+                probabilities = self.predict(x)
+                for k, label in enumerate(self.labels):
+                    error = probabilities[label] - float(y == label)
+                    for j, value in enumerate(x):
+                        gradients[k][j] += error * value
+            rate = 0.3 / math.sqrt(1.0 + step / 80.0)
+            for k in range(len(self.labels)):
+                for j in range(len(xs[0])):
+                    penalty = 0.0 if j == 0 else self.l2 * self.weights[k][j]
+                    self.weights[k][j] -= rate * (gradients[k][j] + penalty) / n
+        return self
+
+    def predict(self, x: Sequence[float]) -> Dict[str, float]:
+        scores = [sum(w * v for w, v in zip(row, x)) for row in self.weights]
+        top = max(scores)
+        exp = [math.exp(value - top) for value in scores]
+        total = sum(exp)
+        return {label: value / total for label, value in zip(self.labels, exp)}
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FamilyModel:
+    candidates: List[str]
+    outcome_model: BinaryLogit
+    propensity_model: Softmax
+    counts: Dict[str, int]
+    context_p90: int
+
+    def augmented(self, base: Sequence[float], model: str) -> List[float]:
+        values = list(base)
+        for candidate in self.candidates[1:]:
+            active = float(model == candidate)
+            values.append(active)
+            values.extend(active * value for value in base[1:])
+        return values
+
+    def risk(self, trajectory: Trajectory, model: str) -> float:
+        return self.outcome_model.predict(self.augmented(trajectory.features, model))
+
+    def propensity(self, trajectory: Trajectory) -> Dict[str, float]:
+        return self.propensity_model.predict(trajectory.features)
+
+
+def fit_models(trajectories: Sequence[Trajectory], official: bool = False) -> Dict[str, FamilyModel]:
+    fitted: Dict[str, FamilyModel] = {}
+    for family, configured in FAMILY_CANDIDATES.items():
+        rows = [t for t in trajectories if t.split == "train" and t.family == family]
+        counts = Counter(t.logged_model for t in rows)
+        candidates = [model for model in configured if counts[model] >= MIN_MODEL_OBS]
+        if len(candidates) < 2:
+            raise ValueError("not enough supported %s models: %r" % (family, counts))
+        eligible = [t for t in rows if t.logged_model in candidates]
+        template = FamilyModel(candidates, BinaryLogit(), Softmax(candidates), dict(counts), 0)
+        xs = [template.augmented(t.features, t.logged_model) for t in eligible]
+        ys = [t.outcome.official_failure if official else t.outcome.observed_failure for t in eligible]
+        outcome_model = BinaryLogit().fit(xs, ys)
+        propensity = Softmax(candidates).fit(
+            [t.features for t in eligible], [t.logged_model for t in eligible],
+        )
+        contexts = sorted(call.input_tokens + call.tools_tokens for t in eligible for call in t.calls)
+        p90 = contexts[min(int(0.9 * len(contexts)), len(contexts) - 1)]
+        fitted[family] = FamilyModel(candidates, outcome_model, propensity, dict(counts), p90)
+    return fitted
+
+
+def choose_initial(trajectory: Trajectory, model: FamilyModel, pricing: Dict[str, Sequence[float]], margin: float = QUALITY_MARGIN) -> Tuple[str, List[str], Dict[str, float]]:
+    risks = {candidate: model.risk(trajectory, candidate) for candidate in model.candidates}
+    propensities = model.propensity(trajectory)
+    best = min(risks.values())
+    ordered = sorted(model.candidates, key=lambda candidate: price_of(candidate, pricing)[0])
+    for candidate in ordered:
+        if propensities.get(candidate, 0.0) >= MIN_PROPENSITY and risks[candidate] <= best + margin:
+            reasons = ["cheapest-supported", "within-2pp-risk"]
+            reasons.extend(name for name, value in trajectory.feature_values.items() if value and name.startswith("intent_"))
+            return candidate, reasons, risks
+    fallback = trajectory.logged_model if trajectory.logged_model in model.candidates else min(risks, key=risks.get)
+    return fallback, ["out-of-support-fallback"], risks
+
+
+def _dynamic_flags(trajectory: Trajectory, call_index: int, context_p90: int) -> List[str]:
+    if call_index <= 0:
+        return []
+    current = trajectory.calls[call_index]
+    prior_items = current.input_items
+    outputs = [
+        item for item in prior_items if isinstance(item, dict)
+        and item.get("type") in ("function_call_output", "custom_tool_call_output")
+    ]
+    flags = []
+    if outputs and ERROR_RE.search(_tool_output_text(outputs[-1])):
+        flags.append("prior-tool-error")
+    signatures = []
+    for item in prior_items:
+        if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("type") in ("function_call", "custom_tool_call"):
+            signatures.append(_tool_name(item))
+    if len(signatures) >= 2 and signatures[-1] == signatures[-2]:
+        flags.append("repeated-tool")
+    if current.input_tokens + current.tools_tokens > context_p90:
+        flags.append("context-p90")
+    if any(item.get("role") == "user" for item in trajectory.calls[call_index - 1].environment_delta if isinstance(item, dict)):
+        flags.append("user-follow-up")
+    return flags
+
+
+def make_routes(trajectory: Trajectory, model: FamilyModel, pricing: Dict[str, Sequence[float]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    initial, reasons, risks = choose_initial(trajectory, model, pricing)
+    certified = [initial] * len(trajectory.calls)
+    adaptive = [initial]
+    adaptive_reasons = {0: list(reasons)}
+    switched = False
+    current = initial
+    for index in range(1, len(trajectory.calls)):
+        flags = _dynamic_flags(trajectory, index, model.context_p90)
+        if flags and not switched:
+            current_price = price_of(current, pricing)[0]
+            stronger = [candidate for candidate in model.candidates if price_of(candidate, pricing)[0] > current_price]
+            if stronger:
+                best = min(model.risk(trajectory, candidate) for candidate in stronger)
+                supported = [
+                    candidate for candidate in stronger
+                    if model.propensity(trajectory).get(candidate, 0.0) >= MIN_PROPENSITY
+                    and model.risk(trajectory, candidate) <= best + QUALITY_MARGIN
+                ]
+                if supported:
+                    current = min(supported, key=lambda candidate: price_of(candidate, pricing)[0])
+                    switched = True
+                    adaptive_reasons[index] = ["one-way-escalation"] + flags
+        adaptive.append(current)
+    return {
+        "certified": certified, "adaptive": adaptive, "initial_reasons": reasons,
+        "adaptive_reasons": adaptive_reasons, "risks": risks,
+    }
+
+
+def route_cost(trajectory: Trajectory, route: Sequence[str], pricing: Dict[str, Sequence[float]], include_observed_final: bool = False, output_ratios: Optional[Dict[str, float]] = None) -> Tuple[float, float]:
+    total = switch_penalty = 0.0
+    for index, (call, selected) in enumerate(zip(trajectory.calls, route)):
+        same = index > 0 and route[index - 1] == selected
+        cacheable = min(call.cacheable_tokens, call.input_tokens + call.tools_tokens) if same else 0
+        pu, pc, po = price_of(selected, pricing)
+        billed = call.input_tokens + call.tools_tokens
+        output_tokens = call.output_tokens if (include_observed_final or not call.is_final) else 0
+        if output_ratios and selected != trajectory.logged_model:
+            denominator = max(output_ratios.get(trajectory.logged_model, 1.0), 0.1)
+            output_tokens = int(output_tokens * output_ratios.get(selected, 1.0) / denominator)
+        total += ((billed - cacheable) * pu + cacheable * pc + output_tokens * po) / 1e6
+        if index > 0 and route[index - 1] != selected:
+            switch_penalty += call.cacheable_tokens * (pu - pc) / 1e6
+    return total, switch_penalty
+
+
+def output_length_ratios(trajectories: Sequence[Trajectory]) -> Dict[str, float]:
+    by_model: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}
+    for trajectory in trajectories:
+        if trajectory.split != "train":
+            continue
+        values = [call.output_tokens for call in trajectory.calls if not call.is_final]
+        if values:
+            by_model.setdefault(trajectory.logged_model, []).append(sum(values) / len(values))
+    means = {model: statistics.fmean(values) for model, values in by_model.items()}
+    ratios: Dict[str, float] = {}
+    for family in FAMILY_CANDIDATES:
+        family_values = [value for model, value in means.items() if _family(model) == family]
+        median = statistics.median(family_values) if family_values else 1.0
+        for model, value in means.items():
+            if _family(model) == family:
+                ratios[model] = min(max(value / median, 0.5), 2.0)
+    return ratios
+
+
+def _effective_n(weights: Sequence[float]) -> float:
+    return (sum(weights) ** 2 / sum(value * value for value in weights)) if weights else 0.0
+
+
+def estimate_policy(trajectories: Sequence[Trajectory], fitted: Dict[str, FamilyModel], actions: Dict[str, str], official: bool, seed_suffix: str = "") -> Dict[str, float]:
+    contributions: List[float] = []
+    weights: List[float] = []
+    covered = 0
+    for trajectory in trajectories:
+        model = fitted[trajectory.family]
+        if trajectory.logged_model not in model.candidates:
+            continue
+        action = actions.get(trajectory.trajectory_id, trajectory.logged_model)
+        if action not in model.candidates:
+            action = trajectory.logged_model
+        propensities = model.propensity(trajectory)
+        action_propensity = propensities.get(action, 0.0)
+        if action_propensity < MIN_PROPENSITY:
+            action = trajectory.logged_model
+        else:
+            covered += int(action != trajectory.logged_model)
+        outcome = trajectory.outcome.official_failure if official else trajectory.outcome.observed_failure
+        mu_policy = model.risk(trajectory, action)
+        mu_logged = model.risk(trajectory, trajectory.logged_model)
+        propensity = max(propensities.get(trajectory.logged_model, 0.0), MIN_PROPENSITY)
+        residual = (outcome - mu_logged) / propensity if action == trajectory.logged_model else 0.0
+        contributions.append(mu_policy + residual - outcome)
+        if action == trajectory.logged_model:
+            weights.append(1.0 / propensity)
+    estimate = statistics.fmean(contributions) if contributions else 0.0
+    rng = random.Random(SEED + seed_suffix)
+    boots = []
+    for _ in range(BOOTSTRAPS):
+        sample = [contributions[rng.randrange(len(contributions))] for _ in contributions]
+        boots.append(statistics.fmean(sample))
+    boots.sort()
+    upper = boots[min(int(0.95 * len(boots)), len(boots) - 1)] if boots else estimate
+    return {
+        "failure_delta": estimate,
+        "failure_upper95": upper,
+        "evaluation_n": len(contributions),
+        "routed_coverage": covered / len(contributions) if contributions else 0.0,
+        "effective_n": _effective_n(weights),
+    }
+
+
+def _proposal_priority(trajectory: Trajectory, route_data: Dict[str, Any], pricing: Dict[str, Sequence[float]]) -> Tuple[float, float]:
+    initial = route_data["certified"][0]
+    risks = route_data["risks"]
+    risk_delta = risks[initial] - risks.get(trajectory.logged_model, risks[initial])
+    logged, _ = route_cost(trajectory, [trajectory.logged_model] * len(trajectory.calls), pricing)
+    routed, _ = route_cost(trajectory, route_data["certified"], pricing)
+    return risk_delta, -(logged - routed)
+
+
+def _adopt_actions(trajectories: Sequence[Trajectory], proposals: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], pricing: Dict[str, Sequence[float]], fraction: float) -> Dict[str, str]:
+    changed = [t for t in trajectories if proposals[t.trajectory_id]["certified"][0] != t.logged_model]
+    changed.sort(key=lambda t: _proposal_priority(t, proposals[t.trajectory_id], pricing))
+    take = int(round(fraction * len(changed)))
+    adopted = {t.trajectory_id for t in changed[:take]}
+    return {
+        t.trajectory_id: proposals[t.trajectory_id]["certified"][0] if t.trajectory_id in adopted else t.logged_model
+        for t in trajectories
+    }

+def _frontier(trajectories: Sequence[Trajectory], fitted: Dict[str, FamilyModel], proposals: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], pricing: Dict[str, Sequence[float]], selected_fraction: Optional[float] = None) -> Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], float]:
+    rows = []
+    for step in range(11):
+        fraction = step / 10.0
+        actions = _adopt_actions(trajectories, proposals, pricing, fraction)
+        quality = estimate_policy(trajectories, fitted, actions, official=False, seed_suffix="-%s" % fraction)
+        official = estimate_policy(trajectories, fitted, actions, official=True, seed_suffix="-official-%s" % fraction)
+        logged_cost = routed_cost = adjusted_cost = 0.0
+        ratios = output_length_ratios(trajectories)
+        for trajectory in trajectories:
+            logged_route = [trajectory.logged_model] * len(trajectory.calls)
+            route = [actions[trajectory.trajectory_id]] * len(trajectory.calls)
+            logged_cost += route_cost(trajectory, logged_route, pricing)[0]
+            routed_cost += route_cost(trajectory, route, pricing)[0]
+            adjusted_cost += route_cost(trajectory, route, pricing, output_ratios=ratios)[0]
+        rows.append({
+            "adopt_frac": fraction,
+            "cost_usd_est": round(routed_cost, 4),
+            "behavior_adjusted_cost_usd_est": round(adjusted_cost, 4),
+            "savings_pct": round((1.0 - routed_cost / logged_cost) * 100.0, 2) if logged_cost else 0.0,
+            "proxy_quality": round(1.0 - quality["failure_delta"], 4),
+            "failure_delta": round(quality["failure_delta"], 5),
+            "failure_upper95": round(quality["failure_upper95"], 5),
+            "official_failure_delta": round(official["failure_delta"], 5),
+            "coverage": round(quality["routed_coverage"], 4),
+            "effective_n": round(quality["effective_n"], 1),
+            "selected": False,
+        })
+    if selected_fraction is None:
+        eligible = [row for row in rows if row["failure_upper95"] <= QUALITY_MARGIN]
+        selected = min(eligible, key=lambda row: row["cost_usd_est"]) if eligible else rows[0]
+        selected_fraction = selected["adopt_frac"]
+    selected = min(rows, key=lambda row: abs(row["adopt_frac"] - selected_fraction))
+    selected["selected"] = True
+    return rows, selected["adopt_frac"]

The first real run exposed two important issues, and the artifacts correctly refused to support the planned claim: the risk model sometimes “improved quality” by upgrading Opus to the more expensive Fable, so total cost rose; and the zero-adoption AIPW comparison was not mathematically valid because the fallback policy explicitly uses the configured/logged default model.

I’m correcting the estimand to the one the shipped interface actually implements: downgrade-from-default effects, screened for propensity overlap and estimated with outcome regression plus clustered bootstrap. Zero adoption will be exactly zero, upgrades will be prohibited, and the deck will name the method accurately.

+# Routemaxxing
+
+Routemaxxing minimizes estimated, cache-aware model cost subject to a two-percentage-
+point upper bound on automatic failure-proxy degradation. It runs fully offline and
+uses only information available before each routing decision.
+
+## The structural finding
+
+The public chunk contains 1,000 unique histories. Their item sequences unfold into
+10,845 model turns: model-authored runs produce tool calls or prose, and environment
+items close one call and begin the next. The briefing-compatible analysis treats the
+last output of every trajectory as unobservable.
+
+The two model families also have disjoint tool dialects. Claude histories expose
+`bash`/`file_edit`; GPT histories expose `shell_command`/`apply_patch`. Routemaxxing
+therefore routes only within a family rather than inventing an unsupported cross-family
+counterfactual.
+
+## Policy
+
+The certified policy reads the opening task, trigger, toolset, initial size, images, and
+nameable intent flags. It chooses the cheapest propensity-supported model whose fitted
+failure risk is within two points of the best supported model, but never upgrades above
+the configured default. It then keeps that model for the whole trajectory to preserve
+the provider cache.
+
+The adaptive policy starts from the certified choice and may escalate once after an
+observed tool error, repeated action, or high-risk context growth. It never downgrades
+or exceeds the original default. Its result is explicitly conditional on logged states:
+a different early model could have generated a different later context.
+
+## Evaluation
+
+- Deterministic 70/30 split grouped by recoverable thread identity, falling back to the
+  stable trajectory hash.
+- L2 logistic outcome models and multinomial propensity models trained on the public
+  training split.
+- Downgrade-from-default effects estimated with propensity-screened outcome regression;
+  unsupported actions fall back to the configured model.
+- Two thousand trajectory bootstrap replicates provide the one-sided 95% upper bound.
+- Cost includes estimated uncached input, cached prefix reads, and every observable
+  output. A switch resets the accumulated cache. Tokens are serialized JSON chars/4,
+  never measured usage.
+- The sensitivity columns remove terminal assistant language from the quality proxy and
+  adjust output length using training-split model ratios.
+
+The automatic failure proxy combines terminal inability language, an unresolved final
+tool error, and repeated identical-action loops. It is not ground-truth task quality.
+The organizer-held-out split is not present yet, so public-validation numbers must not
+be presented as final held-out results.

content.text:
Training-only audit confirms a defensible improvement path:

- Every supported downgrade currently has strong target propensity (minimum about 0.24); support—not propensity—is not blocking it.
- The old “within 2 points of the best model” gate blocks 92 Opus→Sonnet, 24 Fable→Sonnet, and 12 Sol→Terra training proposals, even though Opus→Sonnet is predicted to improve the proxy relative to the configured Opus default.
- GPT Luna has only **12 training trajectories**, below the fixed minimum of 20, so partial pooling cannot make it an eligible action without weakening the support rule.
- Some legacy Claude defaults are currently routed even though their logged action lacks model support; the improved certified policy will correctly keep those defaults.

Proposed change before editing: generate only within-family, cheaper, positive-fixed-and-adjusted-savings downgrades relative to the configured default; rank them by estimated dollars saved per unit of predicted failure risk; and select the quality-margin/adoption combination entirely on training data using the existing 2,000-bootstrap upper bound and ESS floor. I’ll add enriched opening-only features and stronger pooled regularization as an explicit ablation, but only adopt it if its training-only behavior-adjusted cost wins. This expands supported coverage by removing an overly conservative estimand mismatch, not by lowering propensity or ESS requirements.

The richer opening features and propensity pooling reached the same routes but did not justify claiming extra cost savings.

content.text: I found and am correcting an important leakage before accepting the result: the first draft ranked savings using each trajectory’s realized future depth and outputs. That violates the call-zero feature rule even though its quality model did not. I’m replacing it with a training-only, partially pooled savings predictor keyed by opening intent, initial size, trigger, image, and surface; realized trajectory shape will be used only afterward for evaluation.

Implemented and committed on `routemaxing`.

| Public validation | Fixed-shape cost | Behavior-adjusted | Savings | Failure upper95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Logged behavior | $88.88 | $88.88 | — | — |
| Corrected heuristic | $74.68 | $74.64 | 15.97% | −0.01 pp |
| Current certified | $68.98 | $68.84* | 22.39% | −0.19 pp |
| Improved certified | **$48.18** | **$47.90** | **45.79%** | **−0.19 pp** |
| Adaptive, conditional | $79.53 | $79.44 | 10.52% | Not causally estimated |

\*Current router repriced with the new output-length sensitivity for a fair comparison.

The improved router saves another $20.80 fixed-shape and $20.95 behavior-adjusted. Coverage rises from 41.7% to 58.3%, with ESS 155.4 and minimum target propensity 0.255.

Key changes:

- Training-only dollars-per-proxy-risk proposal ranking.
- No future depth, outputs, tool calls, or errors in certified decisions.
- Same-family, whole-trajectory downgrades only.
- Unsupported defaults remain unchanged.
- Luna excluded: 12 training examples versus 20 required.
- Adaptive escalation uses an explicit cache break-even check and remains separately reported.
- Primary proxy excludes the unobservable final answer. The terminal-language sensitivity upper95 is −0.76 pp.
- Enriched features and partial pooling were retained as ablations; they found the same routes, so the simpler policy won.

Verification: 55 tests and 21 subtests pass. All 1,000 routes and 10,845 calls join the explorer. `initial_context/` remains untouched.
